northwind-shop.text:
# Ideal customer profile

Who: weekend hikers who buy gear twice a year.
Where they are: outdoor forums and two newsletters.
What they fear: buying gear that fails on the trail.

Assumptions
- Assumption: most buyers are between 28 and 45. Source: none yet, ask the person.

# Market analysis

Three direct competitors found. Each claim below has a source line.

1. Trailhead Goods: free shipping over 50 (https://trailhead.example/shipping, accessed 2026-10-03)
2. Summit Supply: 30-day returns (https://summit.example/returns, accessed 2026-10-03)
3. Claim without a source: the market grows 8 percent a year. Unsourced.

# Voice guide (draft) Tone: practical or adventurous. OPEN-1: which one leads the launch? Words we use: sturdy, tested, trail-ready. Words we avoid: revolutionary, game-changing. This line is plain text on purpose: no markup is rendered and stays text. OPEN-2: should the voice use second person?

# Brand guidelines

Palette: pine green, sand, a warm orange for calls to action.
Logo: the mark stays on a light background.
Typography: one sans family, two weights.

# UX flows

Flow 1: browse, add to cart, check out.
Flow 2: returning customer, one-click reorder.
Empty cart: not designed yet.

# Architecture

A web front end, a small API, one relational database.
Decision: server-side rendering for product pages.
Risk: the checkout page has no empty state.

# Codebase map

src/catalogue: product listing
src/checkout: cart and payment steps
src/account: sign-in and orders
tests/: one folder per area

# Messaging

Core line: gear you do not have to think about.
Proof points: 2-year warranty, free repairs, tested on three trails.

# Content plan, launch week

Mon: announcement post
Wed: behind-the-scenes photos
Fri: customer story
Status: copy for Monday is being written.

# Brief: launch week

Goal: a week of posts and a fix to the checkout page before it.
Done when: posts approved, pull request merged.
Out of scope: paid ads.

# Workbench state

## Checkpoints
milestones

# Codebase map

src/compaction: merges sorted files
src/wal: write-ahead log
src/api: the public interface

# Compaction API

compact(level): merges the files of one level into the next.
Returns the number of bytes freed.
Raises Busy when another compaction runs.

# Brief: compaction page

Goal: one reference page for the compaction API.
Done when: the page is merged.
